thread:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up — we need a crisp decision surface for canary/A-B rollouts + automatic fallback. Specifically: which component authoritatively decides to cut traffic vs local short-circuit? I'm leaning toward a confidence-score handoff rather than boolean leases. Thoughts?

nina: I like the confidence-score idea. Instead of 'lease valid/invalid' we exchange a small struct: {policy_version, seed, confidence_percent}. Router/runtime then combine local observation into a final score. If combined_confidence < threshold -> fallback.

raju: Agree but keep it tiny. Concrete proposal: controller emits policy with two numbers: baseline_pct and controller_confidence (0-100). Router computes observed_confidence = controller_confidence * controller_weight + local_health_score * local_weight. Default weights: controller_weight=0.7, local_weight=0.3. If observed_confidence < 60 -> route to fallback.

carmen: Operationally, we must ensure auditable decisions. Every final decision should emit a single-line audit event: "ts node policy_v final_score action reason_codes" and we must keep sampling of request_id for privacy. No large payloads.

alex: Tradeoffs: weights and threshold tuning will determine how quickly we fail back. We need safe defaults (conservative: favor fallback) but allow aggressive modes per-team. Also need a "simulate" mode where router logs decisions but doesn't enforce — for ramp testing.

nina: Implementation notes: policy payload format should be versioned JSON or proto v1. Fields: policy_id, seed, baseline_pct, controller_confidence, ttl_seconds, mode(enum: enforce|simulate|drain). Router caches policy until ttl; if ttl expired we enter degraded-mode where local heuristics dominate and controller_confidence=0.

raju: Local heuristics: keep them simple — sliding-window error rate, 95th latency percentile, and a short circuit on OOM/exception spike. Example pseudo: 

```
if local_exception_spike:
  action = fallback
elif local_err_rate_30s > 0.03 or p95_latency > 1200ms:
  action = downgrade_fractional(50%)
else:
  action = follow_controller_pct
```

carmen: We should also define clear backoff for switching variants to avoid oscillation: require a min_stable_window (e.g., 2m) before switching back to new variant and a cool-down after fallback of e.g., 5m. These should be part of the policy.

deploybot: policy-applier: policy "canary-2026-03-22-2" v2 deployed to ap-south-1 at 2026-03-22T12:00:01Z

alex: Observability requirements: rollouts need three signal tiers: (1) high-cardinality sampled events (1% requests) for debug, (2) low-cardinality aggregates per policy/region/min, (3) alerts on signal divergence (controller vs aggregated runtime). We'll expose a debug endpoint: GET /_rollout/debug?policy_id=X&sample=true returning last 100 local decisions (op-safety only).

nina: On API semantics: router should provide decision codes to callers so upper layers can react: DECISION_OK (followed variant), DECISION_FALLBACK, DECISION_SIMULATED, DECISION_DEGRADED. These map to numeric codes so dashboards can aggregate easily.

raju: Hedging: suggest single one-shot hedge attempt to fallback variant with a tight budget (max 40ms), logged as "hedge_attempt". If hedge succeeds, prefer hedged response but still emit an event so controller can learn. Keep hedging off by default, opt-in per-policy.

carmen: Security/privacy: don't send raw prompt/content in audit events. Only include request hash and sampled request_id. Also TTL for audit logs should be configurable per-org.

alex: Edge case: controller rollout policy updated while routers are partitioned. We need deterministic mapping so traffic split is reproducible. Use policy.seed + request_trace_id hashing to decide variant if local heuristics can't reach a decision. Documented pseudo: variant = hash(seed || request_id) % 100 < baseline_pct -> new else old.

nina: Nice. Action items: (1) nina: draft compact policy proto + simulate mode + field semantics (2) raju: implement local heuristics lib + small sim harness to test weights/thresholds (3) carmen: audit event schema + sampling knobs + retention notes. I'll fold into RFC and add sequence diagrams for normal flow and partition handling.

raju: I'll also add experiment results: weight sensitivity sweep and hedging latency cost.

carmen: I'll include an example debug JSON and the minimal audit line spec.

alex: Thanks folks. Plan: merge follow-up RFC draft by EOD Friday, then 1-week pilot in simulate mode for a low-risk model. /cc @nina @raju @carmen
